shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have equal quantities (1 each) of A, C, B. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B - reducing variety and giving me duplicates while losing a good entirely. This decreases my utility since I value variety across all three goods equally.

Currently I have 1 of each good, a perfectly balanced bundle. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and thus utility. I'd rather keep balance or trade in a way that maintains or improves diversity.

This trade would leave me with 3A, 1C, 0B, which is heavily skewed toward A and eliminates B entirely. Since I value variety, going from a balanced 1/1/1 to 3/1/0 reduces my utility despite gaining more total goods. I'd rather keep balance or trade for C instead.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my C for B would just shift the imbalance (2 B, 0 C) instead of improving variety. Since I value variety, this trade doesn't help me.

My current inventory is 1A/1C/1B, perfectly even. Trading away a B for a C would just shift the imbalance from C to B (giving me 1A/2C/0B), not improving variety - it would actually create a new deficit in B. Since I value variety and already have equal amounts, this trade doesn't increase my utility.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 3 C, 0 B - creating imbalance and losing variety, which reduces my utility despite gaining quantity in C.

Trading away my only A to get a second B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B — reducing variety and going to zero on one good. Since I value variety and currently hold equal amounts (1 each), this trade would decrease my utility rather than increase it.

Current inventory is balanced at 1 each (A:1, C:1, B:1). Trading away my only B for a 2nd A would make me imbalanced (A:2, C:1, B:0), reducing variety value. Since I value variety, I should not give up my only unit of a good.

Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating a worse imbalance (variety matters). Current bundle is 1/1/1 which is balanced; ending up with 3A,1C,0B reduces variety value more than gaining an extra A helps. I'd prefer a trade that doesn't eliminate a good entirely.

I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my C for B would just shift the imbalance from B to C without improving variety, since I'd end up with 2 B and 0 C. This doesn't increase my utility given my preference for variety.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only B for another C would make my bundle 1A/2C/0B, reducing variety and leaving me with zero B, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

Trading away my only B (giving up variety, going to 0 B) for a third C creates a lopsided bundle (0 B, 3 C, 1 A), which hurts my variety-based utility more than gaining a duplicate C helps. Better to seek a trade that doesn't zero out a good.

Current inventory is A:1, C:2, B:0. Giving away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, just shifting scarcity rather than improving variety balance. Trading A(1)->B(1) keeps me at one good with 0 and another with 1, same imbalance. Better to seek a trade that adds B while keeping A, e.g. trading a C for a B, which would improve variety more (A:1,C:1,B:1).
I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety, moving from (A1,C2,B0) to (A1,C1,B1), which is a more balanced and higher-utility bundle under my variety-preferring preferences.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 - losing all C entirely, which hurts my variety preference. Trading 1C for 1B instead would be more balanced. This exact trade over-concentrates my loss in C, so I'll decline and propose a better ratio.
Trading 1 A (I have 3) for 1 B (I have only 1) balances my inventory toward A:2, C:1, B:2, increasing variety-based utility.
I already have 3 A and only 1 B and 1 C. This trade would give me even more A (4) while dropping my B to 0, worsening variety. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with only 1 A, 1 C, 2 B - overcorrecting variety in the wrong direction. Current A=3, B=1, C=1; trading 2A for 1B makes B=2 while A drops to 1, C stays lowest at 1. This doesn't balance my holdings well and costs me too much A for one B. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead.

I already have 3 A, so gaining more A while giving up my only extra B (leaving me with 0 B) would worsen my variety balance. This trade would push me further from an even distribution, decreasing my utility.

I currently have equal amounts of C and B (1 each), so trading away my only C for B would just swap which good is scarce without improving variety. I'd end up with 0 C and 2 B, making my bundle less balanced (3 A, 0 C, 2 B) instead of more balanced. I'd rather keep both C and B and seek a trade that reduces my A surplus instead.

Currently I have equal amounts of C and B (1 each), so trading B for C would just swap which good is scarce, not improve variety. Since A is my most abundant good, I'd rather trade away A instead of B. This specific trade doesn't increase my utility.

Current inventory: A:3, C:1, B:1. Trading away my only extra B (I'd drop to 0 B) for 2 C (going to 3 C) would leave me with A:3, C:3, B:0 - losing variety entirely in B while overloading C. This hurts my variety-based utility since I'd have zero of one good. Better to seek a trade that doesn't eliminate a good entirely.
I have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes my variety-based utility.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1C, 1B — trading away my most plentiful good entirely while only gaining one unit of a new good. This overcorrects; a 1-for-1 trade would better preserve variety and value. I'd rather propose or wait for a trade of 1A for 1B instead.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting the variety imbalance rather than fixing it. Current inventory (2A,1C,0B) means I value B and C similarly low; giving up my sole C for B doesn't improve diversity, it just swaps which good I have zero of. I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that adds B without depleting C entirely, or trade from my A surplus instead.
I currently have 0 B, 3 A, and 3 C. Trading away 1 A (reducing to 2, still plenty) for 1 B (going from 0 to 1) improves variety and balances my inventory, increasing overall utility.

Giving up 2 A for only 1 B would leave me with A:1, C:3, B:1 - overly reducing my A stock while only slightly increasing variety. A better ratio like 1A for 1B would improve balance without such a steep cost. Current offer is too unfavorable to my diversified holdings.
I currently have 0 B and 3 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my bundle toward equal holdings, increasing my utility.
Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:3, C:1, B:1, which is too skewed - I'd lose more variety value in C than I'd gain in B. A 1-for-1 trade would be more balanced and acceptable.
I have 0 A, 0 B, 3 C. Trading away a C (which I have plenty of) for a B (which I have none of) improves variety and balances my inventory, increasing utility.
Giving up 2C for 1B leaves me with A:0, C:1, B:1 - still zero A, and I'm giving away too much C value for just one B. A 1-for-1 trade would be more balanced given my preference for variety.
Currently I have 3 A, 1 C, 1 B - heavily skewed toward A. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to 2 A, 1 C, 2 B, which is more balanced and increases variety-weighted utility.
I already have 3 A's and only 1 B and 1 C. Trading away my only B for another A would worsen my variety balance, reducing utility further since B is my scarcest good.

Current inventory: A=3, C=1, B=1. Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me A=1, C=1, B=2 — dropping A below C and creating a new imbalance while only slightly improving B's count. Losing 2A is too much for gaining just 1B; I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade to balance my holdings more evenly.

I already have 3 A, so gaining 2 more A gives diminishing value, while giving up my only spare B (I'd drop to 0 B) reduces my variety significantly. This trade would worsen my balance across goods, so I decline.

Currently I have C:1 and B:1, equal amounts. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with C:0, B:2, A:3, making my bundle more imbalanced (0-2-3) rather than better, which reduces variety-based utility.

Currently I have A:3, C:1, B:1. Trading away my only extra B for C would leave me with C:2, B:0, worsening variety balance since I'd go from having equal low counts of C and B to zero B. This reduces diversity rather than improving it, so I'll decline this specific trade.

Current inventory: A3, C1, B1. Trading away my only extra B (leaving me 0 B) to get C up to 3 would make my bundle A3, C3, B0 - losing variety entirely in B, which is worse given I value variety. Better to keep B and seek a trade that doesn't zero out a good.

I currently have 1 A, 2 C, 0 B. Giving up my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, still an unbalanced bundle (0,2,1), which isn't better than trading for something that improves variety without losing my only unit of a good. Better to seek a trade that doesn't zero out A while gaining B, e.g. trading C for B instead.
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading away 1 C for 1 B moves me toward a more balanced bundle (1 A, 1 C, 1 B), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving away 2C for 1B would leave me with 0 C, going from a balanced-ish bundle (1A,2C,0B) to (1A,0C,1B) - trading two of a good for one of another I lack is inefficient. A 1-for-1 trade would be preferable to maintain variety without depleting C entirely.
Current inventory is A:2, C:2, B:1 - B is my scarcest good. Trading 1 A (which I have more of) for 1 B moves me toward A:1, C:2, B:2, improving balance/variety and increasing overall utility.

I currently have B:1, the good I have least of. Giving up my only scarce B for another A (which I already have 2 of) would worsen my variety balance, reducing utility. Rejecting to preserve B and seek a better trade.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with only 0A, which creates a severe imbalance (0,2,2). Current bundle is (2,2,1). Trading 2A for 1B is too steep - I'd rather trade 1A for 1B to balance toward (1,2,2). This exact trade over-concentrates my losses in A.

This trade would leave me with 4 A, 2 C, 0 B - losing my only B entirely, which hurts variety since B would go from scarce to zero. Since I value variety, going from having 1 of each less-common good to having 0 B while stacking up on A (already my most plentiful) reduces utility rather than increasing it.

Current inventory is A:2, C:2, B:1, so B is my scarcest good and C is tied for most plentiful. Trading away 1 C (reducing to 1) for 1 B (increasing to 2) balances my bundle to A:2, C:1, B:2, improving variety-weighted utility.
I currently have 2C and only 1B. Trading away my only B (my scarcest good) for another C (which I already have 2 of) would worsen my variety balance, decreasing utility.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:2, C:0, B:2 - losing all variety in C which I value for diversity. Current C:2,B:1 gives more balance; trading 2C away is too costly. A better trade would be 1C for 1B to balance without eliminating a good entirely.

This trade would leave me with A:2, C:4, B:0, giving me zero of a good, which hurts my variety-based utility. My current inventory is already balanced (2,2,1); giving up my only B for more C (which I already have) reduces diversity significantly.
